bull.b: Starting a global Phase III trial materially advances pemvidutide toward potential commercialization in MASH. Broad site coverage and a defined 52-week biopsy endpoint create a structured path to generating pivotal efficacy evidence.

bull.t: Positive AUD and ALD clinical progress
bull.b: Clinical activity across AUD and ALD diversifies pemvidutide’s potential indications. Positive drinking-behavior, biomarker and weight-loss outcomes support differentiation, while completed ALD enrollment advances another important liver-disease catalyst.

A well-capitalized, low-leverage balance sheet reduces near-term solvency pressure and supports continued investment in pivotal trials. Management says existing cash funds PERFORMA through its 52-week readout, improving development continuity.

bear.b: Altimmune has negligible product revenue and a cost base dominated by research and development. Sustained annual cash outflows mean value creation depends on successful clinical development and eventual financing or commercialization.

bear.t: Funding gap for potential AUD Phase III
bear.b: A pivotal AUD program would require additional capital beyond the currently funded MASH plan. Reliance on royalties, debt or partnerships introduces execution and dilution risk if non-dilutive funding is unavailable or delayed.

Gastrointestinal tolerability could limit adherence or commercial uptake, while competing Phase III programs may slow enrollment and raise costs. Long timelines also leave substantial regulatory, efficacy and execution uncertainty before approval.
